_what: Sheets whose answers cannot be attributed to the propositions they answer: pair-consistency is at chance under BOTH the item-id mapping and the slot mapping, so the record does not say which proposition each answer belongs to. DECLARED here so the exclusion is a stated limitation rather than an unexplained hole. check_sheet_attribution.py reads this file; an undeclared sheet blocks and a moved count blocks.
_why_this_is_not_loosening_the_gate: floor_table.py already drops these sheets from every row that depends on item identity and counts the drop. Declaring them changes no published number; it makes the exclusion readable, and makes a CHANGE in it fail.
_who_loses_sheets_this_way: Every one of the twelve is a small or quantised build. Eight are local Ollama builds and four are small hosted models; not one frontier model contributes a single unattributable sheet. That is the same split every other defect in this corpus shows, and it is a reason to distrust the LOCAL rows of any table computed without this filter -- not a reason to distrust the filter.
_what_it_is_not: It is not refusal, not truncation and not a parse failure: these sheets arrive complete and well-formed. The record simply does not say whether the model answered by printed item id or straight down the page, and the two readings disagree. A sheet is only ever classified this way when BOTH readings score at chance on the 16 mirrored pairs, so a model holding any position at all is never caught by it.
_denominator: 79 of 5591 valid shuffled sheets, 1.4%. The worst single model is llama3.2:latest at 6 of 13, and the counts per model are below so a reader can drop any model they think is too damaged and recompute.
